name: Partholonians

attributes.attribute: fought the Fomorians in a magic realm

sources: MacAlister, R. A. Stewart. Lebor Gabála Érenn: The Book of the Taking of Ireland, Parts 1–4. Irish Texts Society. Dublin: 1941, Pt. 2, pp. 253–271.
"Pt. 3, pp. 2–102. Partholonians. Irish mythological race. See Partholón."
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Partholonians are a race in the Book of Invasions. They were said to have brought the drink of sovereignty to Ireland. The red ale was called dergfhlaith. The king drank it during his inauguration. A later race, the Tuatha De Danann, refined the brewing. The smith and brewer Goibniu made ale strong enough to give immortality. The Partholonians came to Ireland with their leader Partholon. They fought the monstrous Fomorians in a realm of magic where no blood was shed. They were later destroyed by plague.

okr.objective: Describe the Partholonians and their place in the Book of Invasions.
key_results: The Partholonians brought the ale of sovereignty to Ireland.
They fought the Fomorians in a magical battle without blood.
The race was later destroyed by plague.
